product.name: Portable Bluetooth speaker, 3 speakers + 1 subwoofer (revised design)
product.summary: Revised to the requested layout: three 45 mm full-range speakers (left, centre, right) on the front and one 70 mm subwoofer firing rearward beside a passive radiator, in an enlarged two-piece ABS housing. One main board carries the Bluetooth module, a stereo class-D amplifier for left and right, a mono class-D amplifier for the centre, a boosted class-D amplifier for the subwoofer and a linear Li-ion charger fed from USB-C. Two 18650 cells in parallel supply the amplifiers. The new size and all internal positions are design proposals scaled from the 18650 cells (18 x 65 mm) and the USB-C port (8.9 mm wide), not measurements.
product.powerInput: USB-C, 5 V up to 1 A (charge only)

parts.name: Front grille
parts.function: Protects the three front speakers and lets sound through.
parts.evidence: Grille was visible across the full front face; widened here to suit the larger housing.

parts.name: Front baffle
parts.function: Holds the three front speakers, each in its own sealed rear cup so the subwoofer pressure does not move their cones.
parts.evidence: Original parting line behind the grille; enlarged for three drivers.
parts.unknowns: Rib pattern, rear cups and boss positions are a proposal.

parts.name: Rear housing
parts.function: Main bass chamber. Carries the subwoofer, the passive radiator, the board, the cells, the key board and the port cut-out.
parts.material: ABS, about 2 mm wall, ribbed against bass pressure
parts.process: Injection moulding with side-action for the port opening
parts.evidence: Port cut-out and four screw recesses were visible on the back; depth and width increased to fit the subwoofer.
parts.unknowns: New outer size is a design choice.

parts.name: Passive radiator
parts.function: Unpowered diaphragm tuned with the subwoofer to extend bass from the small sealed volume.
parts.material: Rubber surround with a steel mass plate
parts.evidence: Oval diaphragm was visible through the rear slots; moved to the rear right and enlarged to pair with the subwoofer.
parts.unknowns: Moving mass must be tuned to the final chamber volume.

parts.name: Subwoofer driver
parts.function: 70 mm long-throw woofer, 4 Ω, about 8 W rated, reproduces bass below roughly 150 Hz and fires rearward.
parts.material: Coated paper or PP cone, rubber surround, ferrite magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for one subwoofer. Size, impedance and rear-firing position are design choices.
parts.unknowns: Final driver choice depends on chamber volume. Check Thiele-Small data.

parts.name: Subwoofer rear grille
parts.function: Protects the subwoofer cone on the rear face.
parts.process: Stamped sheet, pressed into a recess
parts.evidence: Needed once a driver is exposed on the rear.

parts.name: Speaker, left
parts.function: Full-range speaker, 45 mm, 4 Ω, driven to about 2 W, left channel above the subwoofer crossover.
parts.material: Paper cone, ferrite magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for three speakers. Left position kept from the original layout.
parts.unknowns: Impedance not confirmed. Measure DC resistance across the terminals.

parts.name: Speaker, centre
parts.function: Full-range speaker, 45 mm, 4 Ω, driven to about 2 W with the left plus right sum.
parts.material: Paper cone, ferrite magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for three speakers. The third is placed as a centre channel.
parts.unknowns: Could instead be wired as a duplicate of one channel. Centre sum is a design choice.

parts.name: Speaker, right
parts.function: Full-range speaker, 45 mm, 4 Ω, driven to about 2 W, right channel above the subwoofer crossover.
parts.material: Paper cone, ferrite magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for three speakers. Right position kept from the original layout.

parts.name: Main board
parts.function: Carries the radio, three amplifiers, the crossover, the charger and all connectors.
parts.material: FR-4, 1.6 mm, 2 layers, green solder mask, HASL finish
parts.process: Single-sided SMT reflow, then hand-soldered wires
parts.evidence: Board edge was visible behind the USB-C opening. Same outline kept, more parts added.
parts.unknowns: Layer count assumed from product class.

parts.name: Bluetooth audio SoC module
parts.function: Bluetooth radio, audio decode, stereo DAC, key scanning, LED control and amplifier enable.
parts.evidence: No marking visible. Typical for this price class.
parts.unknowns: Read the top marking to identify the chip.

parts.name: PCB trace antenna
parts.function: 2.4 GHz meandered inverted-F antenna with a copper keep-out beneath it.
parts.evidence: Typical for module-based designs.
parts.unknowns: The subwoofer magnet and basket now sit about 9 mm above. Check range and retune the match.

parts.name: Crystal, 24 MHz
parts.function: Reference clock for the radio.
parts.evidence: Required by the radio. Frequency assumed.

parts.name: 3.3 V regulator
parts.function: Low-dropout regulator. Drops cell voltage to 3.3 V for the logic and the crossover op-amp.
parts.evidence: A 3.3 V rail is needed from a 3.0 to 4.2 V cell.

parts.name: Crossover and summing op-amp
parts.function: Dual rail-to-rail op-amp: one half sums left and right for the centre speaker, the other is a second-order low-pass at about 150 Hz for the subwoofer.
parts.evidence: The Bluetooth module has only a stereo DAC, so centre and sub feeds must be derived in analogue.
parts.unknowns: Some SoCs can do this in DSP with a third DAC output, which would remove this part.

parts.name: Class-D stereo amplifier (left and right)
parts.function: Filterless bridge-tied-load amplifier, about 2 W per channel into 4 Ω from the cell rail.
parts.evidence: Left and right speakers on a single-cell supply point to a 5 V-class BTL amplifier.

parts.name: Class-D mono amplifier (centre)
parts.function: Filterless mono amplifier, about 2 W into 4 Ω for the centre speaker.
parts.evidence: A third speaker needs a third amplifier channel.

parts.name: Boosted class-D subwoofer amplifier
parts.function: Mono class-D amplifier with built-in boost converter, lifts the cell rail to about 7.5 V and delivers about 5 W into the 4 Ω subwoofer.
parts.package: QFN or ESOP-16 with thermal pad, about 5 × 5 mm
parts.evidence: A 4 Ω subwoofer cannot get useful power from 3.7 V without a boost stage.
parts.unknowns: Exact part and boost voltage to be chosen against the driver rating.

parts.name: Boost inductor, 4.7 µH
parts.function: Energy storage for the subwoofer boost converter, saturation current at least 3 A.
parts.evidence: Required by the boost stage. Sized for about 1.7 A average input with ripple margin.

parts.name: Boost output capacitors, 22 µF
parts.function: Smooth the boosted rail feeding the subwoofer output stage.
parts.evidence: Required by the boost stage.

parts.name: Output ferrite beads
parts.function: Damp switching edges on the eight speaker lines to limit radiated emissions.
parts.evidence: Common with filterless class-D outputs. Count raised from 4 to 8 for four drivers.

parts.name: Bulk capacitor, 470 µF
parts.function: Holds up the cell rail during bass peaks.
parts.evidence: Typical next to class-D amplifiers on a single-cell rail.

parts.name: Li-ion charger
parts.function: Linear constant-current, constant-voltage charger. 4.2 V, about 1 A set by one resistor.
parts.evidence: Single-cell-voltage pack charged from a 5 V port.
parts.unknowns: At 1 A the 4000 mAh pack takes about 5 hours. A switching charger at 2 A would be the upgrade.

parts.name: CC pull-down resistors, 5.1 kΩ
parts.function: Identify the device as a power sink so a USB-C source enables 5 V.
parts.evidence: Required for any USB-C sink that charges from C-to-C cables.

parts.name: USB-C receptacle
parts.function: Charging input. Power-only variant.
parts.evidence: Port visible on the rear face.
parts.unknowns: Whether D+ and D− are routed is not visible.

parts.name: Status LED
parts.function: Shows pairing and charge state through a light pipe.
parts.evidence: Indicator window seen on the original unit. The light pipe is longer in the deeper housing.

parts.name: MEMS microphone
parts.function: Hands-free call microphone, bottom-port.
parts.evidence: Small port hole seen on the original unit.
parts.unknowns: Needs a gasketed sound channel that is isolated from the bass chamber.

parts.name: Key board connector
parts.function: Four-pin header for the key harness.
parts.evidence: Keys sit on a separate board on the top face.

parts.name: Li-ion cell, 18650 (two in parallel)
parts.function: Energy store. 1S2P pack, 3.7 V nominal, about 4000 mAh (14.8 Wh). Second cell added to supply the roughly 3.6 A peak the four amplifier channels draw.
parts.material: Steel can, PVC sleeve, nickel strip links
parts.evidence: Original had one 18650. Peak power budget of about 13 W needs two cells sharing the current.
parts.unknowns: Capacity on the label is often overstated. Measure with a discharge test.

parts.name: Pack protection board
parts.function: Cuts the pack off on over-charge, over-discharge and short circuit. Trip current raised to about 6 A.
parts.package: Small FR-4 strip at the end of the pack
parts.evidence: Expected on any consumer pack. A single FS8205A would trip near 3 A on bass peaks.
parts.unknowns: Confirm over-current threshold with an electronic load.

parts.name: Key board
parts.function: Carries the three tactile switches under the top keypad.
parts.evidence: Three raised keys along the top face. Moved forward to clear the subwoofer basket.

parts.name: Tactile switch
parts.function: Power and play, volume down, volume up.
parts.evidence: Three keys with a click feel.

parts.name: Silicone keypad
parts.function: Sealed key caps that press the switches through the top wall.
parts.evidence: Soft raised keys on the top face.

parts.name: Housing screw
parts.function: Clamp the rear housing to the baffle through long corner bosses.
parts.evidence: Four recessed screw heads on the back.
parts.unknowns: A 240 mm wide box under bass pressure may need two extra mid-span screws.

connections.label: VBUS
connections.evidence: Charger input comes straight from the port.

connections.label: VBAT to left/right amplifier
connections.medium: Wire soldered to the B+ pad, then trace
connections.wire: Red, 20 AWG (carries the full 3.6 A pack peak)
connections.evidence: Peak for 2 × 2 W output at about 88 % efficiency. Average is far lower with music.

connections.label: VBAT to centre amplifier
connections.evidence: Peak for 2 W output at about 88 % efficiency.

connections.label: VBAT to boost inductor
connections.evidence: Peak input needed for 5 W at the subwoofer through boost (90 %) and amplifier (89 %).

connections.label: Boost switch node
connections.evidence: Same current as the inductor feed.

connections.label: Boosted rail, PVDD
connections.evidence: 6.25 W in at about 90 % boost efficiency.

connections.label: Speaker out, left
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2 W into 4 Ω.

connections.label: Speaker out, right
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2 W into 4 Ω.

connections.label: Speaker out, centre
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2 W into 4 Ω.

connections.label: Subwoofer out
connections.evidence: RMS values at 5 W into 4 Ω from the 7.5 V boosted rail.

connections.label: Audio, left and right
connections.protocol: Analogue line level, AC coupled (small coupling capacitors high-pass at about 150 Hz)

connections.label: Subwoofer flange screwed and gasketed to the rear wall

controls.label: Power
controls.action: Hold to switch the speaker on or off.

controls.label: Volume down
controls.action: Lowers the volume one step on all three speakers and the subwoofer.

controls.label: Volume up
controls.action: Raises the volume one step on all three speakers and the subwoofer.

unknowns: Your request was read as one subwoofer plus three full-range speakers (left, centre, right), four drivers in total. If you meant three drivers in total, the centre speaker and U4 drop out.
The housing grew from 150 × 64 × 66 mm to about 240 × 84 × 90 mm to fit the drivers. This size and every internal position are proposals, not measurements.
Subwoofer driver choice, chamber volume and passive radiator mass have not been tuned together.
Exact Bluetooth chip, and whether it can do the crossover and centre mix in DSP instead of the op-amp.
Exact boosted amplifier part and boost voltage for the subwoofer.
Real cell capacity and whether the protection board holds the roughly 3.6 A peak without tripping.
Board layer count and whether the USB data lines are routed.
Whether the full-range speakers need separate sealed cups or closed-back drivers to stay isolated from subwoofer pressure.
verifySteps: Confirm the intended driver count and positions (three front speakers plus a rear subwoofer) before tooling changes.
Build a chamber mock-up and measure the subwoofer and passive radiator response to set the crossover frequency.
Measure peak battery current at full volume with bass-heavy music and check the protection board does not trip.
Measure VBAT sag, the 3.3 V rail and the boosted rail with the unit playing.
Check Bluetooth range with the subwoofer fitted above the antenna area.
Read the markings on U1, U2 and U3 under magnification on the original board.
Put a USB power meter in line to confirm input current and full charge time for the two-cell pack.
safety: Two Li-ion cells in parallel inside. Do not pierce, short or heat them. Match cell voltage before joining them and disconnect the pack before soldering.
The pack can deliver well over 10 A into a short. Keep the protection board in circuit.
The boost stage puts about 7.5 V on the subwoofer rail and its inductor and amplifier run warm at full volume.
Discharge the bulk and boost capacitors before probing near the amplifiers.
The subwoofer magnet is strong. Keep it away from loose screws and steel tools while assembling.
